# HInput

> A labeled input with help/error text and native validation. Web components participate in their owning form.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HInput` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-input>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthInputElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HInput.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Supply a visible label and a name for form submission. Use type=email/url/password/number/etc. for native input behavior.
- The model is a string, including type="number". Use HRange for a numeric slider.
- hint/error associate explanatory text with the input; native required, pattern, and length constraints control browser validation. Application error text does not replace backend validation.

## Public API

modelValue, value, label, name, placeholder, hint, error, autocomplete, pattern: string · type: text | email | password | url | search | number | tel · required, disabled, readonly: boolean · minlength, maxlength: number · min, max: string | number

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: string;
    value?: string;
    label: string;
    name?: string;
    type?: "text" | "email" | "password" | "url" | "search" | "number" | "tel";
    placeholder?: string;
    hint?: string;
    error?: string;
    required?: boolean;
    disabled?: boolean;
    readonly?: boolean;
    autocomplete?: string;
    minlength?: number;
    maxlength?: number;
    min?: string | number;
    max?: string | number;
    pattern?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ type: "text", value: "" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(value), change(value)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: string
    ];
    change: [
        value: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, control, hint

Use `hearth-input::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HInput } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
const name = ref('Photos');
</script>

<template>
  <HInput v-model="name" label="Application name" name="appName" required hint="Choose a recognizable name." />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-input');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Application name",
  "name": "appName",
  "value": "Photos",
  "required": true,
  "hint": "Choose a recognizable name."
});
element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});
mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HTextarea](../textarea/llms.txt): A labeled multiline field with native constraints and form reset support.
- [HSelect](../select/llms.txt): A native select with labeled options, not a recreated browser picker.
- [HCombobox](../combobox/llms.txt): Searchable single or multi-select with selected chips, disabled options, keyboard navigation, and repeated form values.
